t: Lady Wen conspires against Tianzuo
c: In the spring of 1121, Tianzuo's second wife, Lady Wen, conspired with her brother in law, General Yelü Yudu, to depose the emperor and enthrone her son.

t: Jin forces capture Central Capital
c: He was allowed to remain in command of his troops and in the winter of 1121–22, he led Jin forces to capture the Central Capital.

t: Commanders defect to Song dynasty
c: In the late autumn of 1122, her commanders Guo Yaoshi and Gao Feng defected with their troops to the Song dynasty.

t: Wuqimai succeeds Aguda as Jin leader
c: After Aguda died in 1123, he was succeeded by his younger brother Wuqimai (posthumously Emperor Taizong of Jin).

t: Jin forces cross Yellow River, besiege Kaifeng
c: The Jin forces crossed the Yellow River in the winter of 1126–27 and laid siege to Kaifeng again.

t: Death of former Song Emperor Huizong
c: Huizong died in 1135 in Wuguocheng, a town near the Songhua River.

t: Song loses Kaifeng but continues resistance
c: The failure of the Song to defend Kaifeng in 1127 did not result in a cessation of conflict or the surrender of the Song.

t: Great Qi capital relocates to Kaifeng
c: At first Great Qi was based at Daming in Hebei, but by 1132, Liu Yu had moved to Kaifeng.

t: Great Qi captures Xiangyang from Song
c: Great Qi's troops fought alongside the Jurchens and even succeeded in beating Song forces a few times, notably capturing Xiangyang in 1135.

t: Yue Fei leads Song offensive recaptures territory
c: But this victory was short lived and the Song offensive led by Yue Fei in 1134–5 ended up recapturing much of the lost Song territory.

t: Death of Jin Emperor Taizong of Jin
c: Liu Yu's patron, Wuqimai, died in 1135 and was succeeded by Hela, a grandson of Emperor Taizu of Jin.

t: Emperor Xizong of Jin succeeds Taizong
c: After Emperor Taizong of Jin died in 1135, he was succeeded by Hela (posthumously Emperor Xizong of Jin), a grandson of Emperor Taizu of Jin.

t: Jin abolishes puppet state Great Qi
c: He demoted Liu Yu from emperor of Great Qi to the rank of prince and abolished the state of Great Qi in 1137.

t: Jin recaptures Shaanxi and Henan
c: In 1140, the Jin retook Shaanxi and Henan and sent troops south of the Yellow River.

t: Southern Song court seeks peace with Jin
c: The Southern Song court, based in Hangzhou since 1138, sought to appease the Jin by eliminating the revanchist faction.

t: Jin invests Khabul Khan as Mongol state ruler
c: In 1146–7, the Jin invested Khabul Khan with the title of assisting state ruler of the Mongols.

t: Jin accuses Song of violating Shaoxing Treaty
c: In 1158, he accused the Song of breaking the Shaoxing Treaty by making illicit purchases of horses at the border markets.

c: Song military leaders started instigating conflict on the Huai River border starting from 1204.

t: Zhangzong promulgates Taihe Code in Jin
c: In 1202, Zhangzong promulgated the Taihe Code to unify existing legislations.

t: Emperor Wanyan Yongji succeeds Zhangzong
c: When Emperor Zhangzong died in 1208, he was succeeded by Shizong's seventh son, Wanyan Yongji (originally Wanyan Yunji).

t: Mongols attack Jin in two directions
c: In the spring of 1211, the Mongols attacked the Jin in two directions.

t: Mongols capture Juyong Pass and devastate Jin territory
c: In the spring of 1212, the Mongols took Juyong Pass again and penetrated deep into Jin territory, devastating parts of Hebei, Shandong, and Shanxi.

t: Genghis defeats Jin army led by Zhuhu Gaoqi
c: Genghis defeated another Jin army led by Zhuhu Gaoqi in the summer of 1213.

t: Yellow River flood prevents Jin campaign in Shandong
c: The Jin were unable to defeat them and in 1217, another Yellow River flood prevented them from taking action in Shandong.

t: Song appoints rebel leader Li Quan as prefect
c: In 1218, the Song appointed the rebel leader Li Quan as commanding prefect of Shandong.

t: Mongol-Song invasion campaign fails
c: Li Quan joined the Mongols in attacking the Song in 1230 but the invasion ended in failure and Li Quan was killed on 18 February 1231.

t: Li Tan defects to Song dynasty
c: Li Quan's adopted son, Li Tan, inherited his father's position and defected to the Song in 1262, for which Kublai Khan had him executed.

t: Mongols destroy rebel Khitan state
c: The rebel Khitan state was destroyed by the Mongols in 1233.

t: Jin assign Puxian Wannu to suppress rebellion
c: In 1214, the Jin assigned Puxian Wannu to suppress the rebellion.

t: Puxian Wannu defeated, then rebels
c: However Puxian Wannu was defeated and he himself rebelled in 1215.

t: Puxian Wannu declares independence from Mongols
c: In 1224, Puxian Wannu declared independence from the Mongols and sent envoys to Goryeo to establish an alliance.

t: Emperor Aizong of Jin succeeds Emperor Xuanzong
c: Ningjiasu, posthumously Emperor Aizong of Jin, succeeded his father, Emperor Xuanzong of Jin, in 1224.

t: Jin and Western Xia conclude peace treaty
c: A peace treaty with the Western Xia was concluded in 1225 acknowledging that the Western Xia was no longer a vassal of the Jin.

t: Death of Genghis Khan
c: When Genghis Khan died in 1227, Aizong tried to appease the Mongols with an embassy offering their condolences, but the Mongols refused to receive their envoys.

t: Siege of Kaifeng begins
c: The Siege of Kaifeng (1232) began on 8 April 1232.

t: Jin use thunder crash bombs against Mongols
c: Heaven-shaking-thunder bombs, also known as thunder crash bombs, had been used in 1231 by a Jin general to destroy a Mongol warship.

t: Mongols besiege Caizhou
c: Caizhou came under siege by the Mongols in December 1233.

t: Kublai becomes Great Khan of Mongols

t: Genghis Khan becomes Great Khan
c: Genghis Khan united the Mongol tribes of the steppes and became Great Khan in 1206.

t: Möngke Khan becomes Great Khan
c: Möngke Khan succeeded Ögedei's son, Güyük, as Great Khan in 1251.

t: Kublai returns to face Ariq Böke challenge
c: Kublai returned from fighting the Song in 1260 when he learned that his brother, Ariq Böke, was challenging his claim to the throne.

t: Li Tan instigates revolt against Mongols
c: Li Tan, the son-in-law of a powerful official, instigated a revolt against Mongol rule in 1262.

t: Kublai claims Mandate of Heaven and declares Yuan

t: General Zhang Hongfan defeats Song loyalists
c: The Yuan forces commanded by Han Chinese General Zhang Hongfan led a predominantly Han navy to defeat the Song loyalists at the battle of Yamen in 1279.

c: Following the conquest of Dali in 1253, the former ruling Duan family were appointed as its leaders.

t: Crown Prince Zhenjin dies before Kublai
c: Kublai originally named his eldest son, Zhenjin, as the crown prince, but he died before Kublai in 1285.

t: Tugh Temür recalled to Khanbaliq
c: When Yesün Temür died in Shangdu in 1328, Tugh Temür was recalled to Khanbaliq by the Qipchaq commander El Temür.

t: Toghon Temür dismisses Toghtogha
c: In 1354, when Toghtogha led a large army to crush the Red Turban rebels, Toghon Temür suddenly dismissed him for fear of betrayal.

t: Han Lin'er dies, Red Turban Song dynasty ends

t: Marco Polo's Travels published
c: The account of his travels, Il milione (or, The Million, known in English as the Travels of Marco Polo), appeared about the year 1299.

t: Buyantu Khan revives imperial exams
c: Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan revived the imperial exams in 1315 with some major alterations.

t: Jade Mirror of the Four Unknowns written
c: His method is described in the Jade Mirror of the Four Unknowns, written in 1303.

t: Wei Yilin invents suspension method for dislocations
c: The physician Wei Yilin invented a suspension method for reducing dislocated joints, which he performed using anesthetics.

t: Jesus the Interpreter founds Office of Western Medicine
c: The Nestorian physician Jesus the Interpreter founded the Office of Western Medicine in 1263 during the reign of Kublai.

t: Mongols establish Imperial Library Directorate
c: In 1273, the Mongols created the Imperial Library Directorate, a government-sponsored printing office.

c: Persian official Yawuna assassinated both Amin ud-Din and Saif ud-Din in 1362 and took control of the Muslim rebel forces.

t: New imperial capital established at Heian-kyō
c: In 794, a new imperial capital was established at Heian-kyō (modern Kyoto), marking the beginning of the Heian period, which lasted until 1185.

t: Tokugawa Ieyasu appointed shōgun
c: After Toyotomi's death in 1598, Tokugawa Ieyasu came to power and was appointed shōgun by the emperor.

t: Portuguese arrive in Japan
c: Portugal and Japan came into contact in 1543, when the Portuguese became the first Europeans to reach Japan by landing in the southern archipelago.

t: Japanese military invades Manchuria
c: The Japanese military invaded Manchuria in 1931, and from 1937 the conflict escalated into a prolonged war with China.

t: Hunter-gatherers arrive in Japan
Buddhism introduced to Japan from Baekje
c: The Asuka period began as early as 538 AD with the introduction of the Buddhist religion from the Korean kingdom of Baekje.

t: Prince Shōtoku serves as regent of Japan
c: Prince Shōtoku, an advocate of Buddhism and of the Soga cause, who was of partial Soga descent, served as regent and de facto leader of Japan from 594 to 622.

t: Prince Naka overthrows Soga clan in coup
c: In 645, the Soga clan were overthrown in a coup launched by Prince Naka no Ōe and Fujiwara no Kamatari, the founder of the Fujiwara clan.

t: Smallpox epidemic devastates Japan
c: Between 812 and 814 CE, a smallpox epidemic killed almost half of the Japanese population.

t: Abe clan openly defies central authority
c: By 1051, members of the Abe clan, who occupied key posts in the regional government, were openly defying the central authority.

t: Later Three-Year War and Northern Fujiwara rise

t: Taira no Kiyomori dies during Genpei War
c: Though Taira no Kiyomori died in 1181, the ensuing bloody Genpei War between the Taira and Minamoto families continued for another four years.

t: Yoritomo dies, shogunate office weakens
c: After Yoritomo's death in 1199, the office of shogun weakened.

t: Hōjō Tokimasa appointed regent to shogun Minamoto no Sanetomo
c: In 1203, her father, Hōjō Tokimasa, was appointed regent to the shogun, Yoritomo's son Minamoto no Sanetomo.

t: Emperor Go-Daigo launches restoration rebellion
c: In 1333, Emperor Go-Daigo launched a rebellion in the hope of restoring full power to the imperial court.

t: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu comes to power

t: Ōnin War breaks out over shogun succession
c: This started in 1467 when the Ōnin War broke out over who would succeed the ruling shogun.

t: Shogun loses power to independent daimyō
c: By the time the succession was settled in 1477, the shogun had lost all power over the daimyō, who now ruled hundreds of independent states throughout Japan.
